axis_convention: axial = +z; origin at the housing leading edge
solved_azimuthal_discretisation: one cell over a 5.0-degree wedge; the solve is axisymmetric
facet_attribute_meaning: the 2-byte STL attribute is the part index into `part_order`
declared_display_choices: 360-degree revolve of an axisymmetric 5-degree wedge solve; the axisymmetry must be stated wherever this surface is shown
azimuthal revolve resolution (180 segments) is a display choice and is not the solved azimuthal discretisation
the flat discs at z = -0.250 and z = 0.500 are the DOMAIN TRUNCATION PLANES at inlet and outlet, drawn only so the centrebody is a closed solid; they are not physical faces
declared_omissions: no nose and no tail: build_t23.py lines 12-18 REMOVE the nose and tail cones of the owner's directive 3.2 and declare the centrebody a constant-radius tube over the whole axial extent. Drawing them would show geometry that was never solved.
no struts: the retired surface carried three radial struts (96 facets, 0/120/240 degrees) that were never solved and that are inconsistent with an axisymmetric solve
the 0.006 m shaft bore is an internal boundary of the core region over z = 0.000..0.125 only; it is not visible on a closed external surface and appears in the cross-section mesh view instead
the duct wall has ZERO THICKNESS because the solved duct wall is a boundary condition with no thickness; the retired surface's 5 mm duct wall was a declared display invention

retires.reason: dimensioned from F28_DUCTED_ACTUATOR_DISK_PREREGISTRATION.md, a different case; 0.200 m axial against the solved 0.750 m; three unsolved struts; nose and tail the solve does not have
